headline: High: shared writable datastore and filesystem make Dify↔Flowise prompt injection, data leakage, and output-cascade risks plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and uses shared state via Dify server datastore; Flowise also reads/writes files and shares state via server datastore. That creates a plausible bridge for one agent’s content to be consumed by the other as trusted input. No MCP or clipboard is needed, but the shared workspace makes injection feasible.
conditions: IF Dify writes attacker-controlled text into shared datastore or uploaded files
IF Flowise reads that shared content as instructions or tool parameters
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces/datastores
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files between the two systems
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent messages
Require manual review before copying outputs across agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch conversation/chatflow inputs and outputs, handle uploaded files, and have broad network egress. If they share a datastore or filesystem, sensitive knowledge-base content or chatflow inputs can flow from Dify into Flowise outputs or backend calls. The profiles do not prove exfiltration by default, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same server datastore or mounted filesystem
IF sensitive knowledge-base files or chatflow inputs are present in that shared location
mitigations: Use separate storage buckets or directories per agent
Restrict file permissions so each agent can only read its own workspace
Turn off automatic upload of file contents to model providers where possible
Redact secrets from shared artifacts before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both Dify and Flowise have write_filesystem and broad network_egress, and both support multiple instances with shared state via server datastore. Concurrent writes to the same directory or mutable workflow state can overwrite each other or corrupt runs. Because the profiles show overlapping write surfaces without locking guarantees, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or datastore
IF no external lock or transaction layer serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories to each agent
Enable filesystem or database locking around shared resources
Run the agents in isolated containers or namespaces
Schedule writes so only one agent mutates shared state at a time

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify and Flowise are both orchestration systems that can pass outputs into tools or downstream nodes. If Flowise consumes Dify-generated text without verification, an error or hallucination can cascade into later actions. The profiles do not show automatic action authority, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Dify output as a prompt, tool argument, or node input
IF no validation step checks Dify’s claims before execution
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Dify and Flowise
Require citations or structured schemas for inter-agent outputs
Log and diff intermediate outputs before downstream execution
Disable automatic tool execution on untrusted text

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source orchestration platforms with similar data classes and no explicit residency or certification mismatch in the profiles. The main compliance risk is policy drift in logging or retention, but the evidence does not show a concrete mismatch. Because no stronger compliance gap is documented, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF the deployment assigns different retention or logging policies to the same data class
IF regulated data is routed through one agent but not the other
mitigations: Align retention settings across both systems
Disable verbose logging for sensitive workflows
Document which data classes each agent may store
Review deployment residency settings before production
